findings.issue: The generic card component renders ability-specific 'Hidden ability' text driven by CardData.hidden, so removing or restyling the Abilities feature means editing a shared component, and every other card consumer carries the field.
findings.suggestion: Generalize to a CardData.note?: string populated only by getAbilityPage, or reuse the existing renderAction-style slot for the note.

findings.issue: Selected-game resolution exists twice: the server already validates ?game against p.games (functions.ts:57) and the client select re-runs p.games.some(...) to pick its value, so changing the default-game rule requires two coordinated edits.
findings.suggestion: Have the server return the resolved game (it already does as p.game) and let the select use search.game ?? p.game, or fold the invalid-URL handling into validateSearch so only one place decides which game is active.

findings.issue: readTeamCookie is exported but never used; the initial team actually arrives via the root loader (functions.ts:43), so this dead helper misleads a reader about how team state reaches the client.
findings.suggestion: Delete readTeamCookie (and encodeTeam if it stays single-use), or document that the cookie is only read on the server.

findings.issue: The typeLabels Map (name → label) is built identically in index.tsx:63 and team.tsx:20, and card types resolve labels on the client while page-level types resolve them server-side — a split seam for one concern.
findings.suggestion: Resolve labels server-side into CardData.types as TypeRef values (or a shared useTypeLabels helper), so the client never maps names to labels.

findings.issue: writeTeamCookie is called inside the setState updater; React updaters can run more than once (StrictMode/concurrent), and side effects there are fragile even though this one is idempotent.
findings.suggestion: Compute the next team outside the updater (or derive the cookie write in an effect keyed on team) so the update stays pure.

findings.issue: getTeamPage calls typeList() twice (for types and typeDetails) — harmless thanks to memo(), but the parallel derivation reads as two independent sources of the same list.
findings.suggestion: Call typeList() once and derive both from the same promise.

findings.issue: spriteUrl reconstructs sprite URLs from the documented pattern on the client instead of threading the API-provided sprites.front_default through CardData, duplicating knowledge the API already carries (though in a single choke point).
findings.suggestion: If the API's sprite scheme ever becomes less predictable, add a sprite field to CardData populated in toCards/speciesIndex/getTeamPage rather than branching the URL builder.

summary: This is a well-layered, idiomatic TanStack Start codebase: routes are thin, server functions own all data shaping, and every Pokémon list funnels through one normalizer and one card component, so most fixes land in a single obvious place. The main editability costs are small: ability-specific semantics baked into the shared card, a couple of two-place duplications (type labels, game selection), and one dead helper. I'd merge it and file the findings as follow-ups.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Delete one route file plus two contiguous server blocks plus the Pokémon page's Abilities section; the nav needs no edit. The awkward part is excising CardData.hidden / 'Hidden ability' from the shared card component, which drags two generic files into an ability-only change.

scenarios.change: Fix the card sprite for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: toCards (pokeapi.ts:96) already normalizes pokémon refs to species IDs in one place, and spriteUrl/PokemonCard is the single sprite choke point, so one fix covers home, moves, abilities, types and team lists. If the fix must use sprites.front_default instead of the ID pattern, CardData gains a field populated in the three producers (toCards, speciesIndex, getTeamPage) — contained and discoverable.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: One opt-in sortBy prop on PokemonCardList implements it; lists already arrive dex-ordered from toCards. The team page must keep insertion order per FEATURE.md, so sorting has to be opt-in, which costs four small call-site edits.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: The data plumbing (fetchJson/memo/list, englishName), the rendering primitives (Section, PokemonCardList, TypeBadge, NotFound) and the server-fn-per-page pattern are all reusable; only a ~10-line getter, one server function and two thin route files are new — inherent file-routing boilerplate rather than copied logic.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: apiBase() and the TTL/memo cache are each defined once in pokeapi.ts; the client learns the media base only via getConfig in the root loader, so a base-URL or TTL change is a one-file edit (plus the automatic forwarding).
